teaching.hint: How can each node find its closest matching ancestor while all decisions still refer to the original tree?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A traversal of the original tree exposes the ancestor path; the nearest same-letter ancestor can be remembered by letter, while reparenting remains only a recorded decision.
solution_outline.approach: Traverse original edges, recording each node's new parent from its current ancestor path. Then aggregate subtree sizes from children to their recorded final parents, using an order in which original descendants come first.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: During the first traversal, per-letter path state contains exactly matching ancestors of the current node. During reverse aggregation, each node's accumulated size covers its complete final subtree.
solution_outline.correctness: Each chosen new parent is an original ancestor, so reverse original preorder processes a child before its final parent. Simultaneous changes use original ancestry throughout, and each final edge contributes its subtree exactly once.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space; iterative traversal avoids recursion overflow on a 100,000-node chain.
solution_outline.pitfall: Changing parent links during ancestor discovery would make later choices depend on an already modified tree.

common_wrong_turns: Process reparenting sequentially on the changing tree
Aggregate sizes in numeric node order
source_fidelity_notes: The original-tree ancestor rule, simultaneous timing, unchanged-parent case, and chain-size bound are explicit.
